edits.new: 20-year distribution concession from 2005. Those were the holdings at the start; by the end of the concession Umeme was listed on the Uganda Securities Exchange and cross-listed in Nairobi, and its 2025 report mentions neither Eskom nor Globeleq. The 20-year concession ended on 31 March 2025, when the network was handed to the state company UEDCL and headcount fell from 2,409 to 18.

Coal miner obliged to resettle. Vale bought the Colombian coal assets in 2008 for US$308 million and by June 2012 had agreed to sell the El Hatillo mine, the Cerro Largo deposit, Sociedad Portuaria Rio Cordoba and 8.43% of the FENOCO railway to Goldman Sachs-controlled Colombia Natural Resources; Murray Energy bought Colombia Natural Resources from Goldman Sachs on 14 August 2015 and renamed the mines Murray Colombian Resources.

Ultimate owner of IEnova. Sempra's own about-us page no longer mentions IEnova; it says Sempra holds a partial interest in Sempra Infrastructure Partners. The description here fits the position at the time of the case.

edits.old: Bought RCA's consumer electronics arm (1988 per the Taipei Times); held liable by Taiwan's courts
edits.new: Bought RCA's consumer electronics arm (1988 per the Taipei Times); held liable by Taiwan's courts. Britannica dates the purchase of General Electric's consumer electronics division, which included RCA, to 1987, and says Thomson Consumer Electronics was created in 1988; the 1988 date matches the naming of the arm rather than the purchase.

Contractor (EJAtlas). On 4 May 2020 the company announced a change of name to Webuild, for approval at that day's shareholders' meeting, as it merged with Astaldi; Salini Impregilo is the name used up to that date.

edits.new: Operator of the Block V exploration. Shareholders approved a change of registered name to Pharos Energy plc on 16 October 2019; SOCO International plc is the name the company used up to that date.
Concession holder. The company announced on 30 April 2024 that it was changing its name to SD Guthrie Bhd; at that date Permodalan Nasional Bhd held 55.1% and the Employees Provident Fund 15.2%.

edits.new: Original Canadian owner that took the land in 2004-2006. Kinross Gold completed its acquisition of all Red Back shares on 17 September 2010 and the shares were delisted from the Toronto Stock Exchange after the close on 21 September 2010, so Red Back no longer exists as a separate listed company. The filing does not state its nationality or head office.

Parent company. A 2014 transaction with PRHI cut TVI Pacific's interest in TVI Resource Development (Phils.) Inc. to 30.66%, after which it concluded it no longer controlled TVIRD and deconsolidated it; parent fits the period up to that transaction.
Majority partner by 2025. Silvercorp's 75% interest in El Domo dates from 31 July 2024, when it completed the acquisition of Adventus Mining Corporation.
Project co-manager. Wildlife Alliance Inc is a 501(c)(3) whose IRS filings give New York; its own history page gives a contact address in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, without calling it a headquarters.

Shareholder (20%). Samtan's other Indonesian position has changed: it was described in June 2011 as holding 49% of the East Kalimantan coal miner PT Kideco Jaya Agung, and after Indika Energy and PT Muji Inti Utama acquired 45% in December 2017 it was left with 9%.

Mine operator. The mine was developed under Rio Tinto, which held 68.62%; the company's own page says China National Uranium Corporation, part of China National Nuclear Corporation, became the majority shareholder in 2019.

Nickel mine and smelter operator. The company's own shareholder page is out of date: it gives MIND ID 20% as at 7 October 2020, but a divestment completed on 28 June 2024 made the state holding company the largest shareholder on about 34%, cutting Vale Canada to about 33.9% and Sumitomo Metal Mining to about 11.5%.

edits.new: Pipeline company, owned by BP, SOCAR and Snam (20% each), Fluxys (19%), Enagás (16%) and Axpo (5%). TAP's own page of 15 November 2025 lists five shareholders at 20% each - bp, SOCAR, Snam, Fluxys and Enagas - and does not name Axpo; the split given here matches an earlier period, and the page does not say when or in what stages it changed.

edits.old: Owner of Cerro Matoso since May 2015
edits.new: Owner of Cerro Matoso since May 2015. South32 held Cerro Matoso at the time of the case; its annual report for the year to 30 June 2025 records a binding agreement of 7 July 2025 to divest the operation for nominal upfront consideration and up to US$100 million in future cash payments, completion expected in late H1 FY26.

edits.old: Owner and builder when the dredging and spill happened; Gazprom took a majority in December 2006 (FoE Japan)
edits.new: Owner and builder when the dredging and spill happened; Gazprom took a majority in December 2006 (FoE Japan). Oil & Gas Journal, dated 24 April 2007, reports the purchase as done: Gazprom paid US$7.45 billion for 50% plus one share, leaving Shell at about 27.5%, Mitsui 12.5% and Mitsubishi 10%. The article gives no signing date, so it neither confirms nor contradicts the December 2006 date given here for the agreement.

edits.old: Indian microfinance lender, which went public in August 2010
edits.new: Indian microfinance lender, which went public in August 2010. A June 2019 stock exchange filing records that the company, renamed Bharat Financial Inclusion Limited, had its assets and liabilities transferred to IndusInd Bank with effect from 4 July 2019, so it ceased to exist as a separate listed lender from that date.

Original lease holder. Shareholders voted on 15 March 2010 to rename the company Vaaldiam Mining Inc on completing its acquisition of Vaaldiam Resources, so the name Tiomin Resources was dropped in 2010. Neither source opened states a Toronto head office, so the headquarters given here is unverified rather than contradicted.

Mining permit holder. Petromindo, reporting on 19 September 2016, describes the company as a joint venture between PT Allindo Indonesia and China's Aempire Resource Ltd, with no split given and no mention of Hong Kong.

edits.new: Malaysian logging group. Oxfam links it to the Turubu lease through shared addresses, directors and shareholders and inquiry findings; the lease holder is Sepik Oil Palm Plantation Ltd. ACT NOW! reports that in May 2021 a Malaysian newspaper carried a statement from WTK Holdings Berhad that it had no logging operations in Papua New Guinea, and that the company did not reply to a request for clarification; ACT NOW! itself links more than 30 PNG-registered companies to the group through common directors and shareholders.

edits.new: Third plant named by the government. China Daily's February 2012 report on the Shanghai municipal government findings gives the full name as Shanghai Kangshuo Waste Recycling Co, a recycler of used goods and materials, whose plant had since relocated.

Mine owner and operator. Philex Mining's own Integrated Annual Corporate Governance Report for 2023 gives the principal office as Reliance corner Sheridan Streets, Mandaluyong City, not Pasig; the filings opened do not say when it moved, so an earlier Pasig address is not excluded.

Shareholder. The company's own background page says it was founded on 7 March 2000 as Ratchaburi Electricity Generating Holding Public Company Limited and is now RATCH Group Public Company Limited; the page does not give the date of the name change.

Parent and operator. Daily Maverick (April 2021) names the operator of the Cato Ridge mercury recovery factory as Thor SA, closed by the government in 1991, after which the group restructured through a demerger; the parent it names is the UK-based Tato Holdings group, which agreed to set aside nearly R174 million for the clean-up.
